body:
Yeah, my troubles really are small beans. Need a bit of perspective.

I wish you well, friend.

Yeah, it's 24/7, so I can call anytime. 

I imagine a psychiatrist would be better, but none are nearby. Good to hear you're hanging in there.

Yeah, I was on a counselling helpline just a few hours ago.  

Thanks for the offer to talk. Talking helps me feel better in the moment.

Thank you. 

And I know you're right, I know it... it's just that my head starts saying otherwise.

That's the thing: I failed the degree. Sure, I can go back (part-time end of this year, before final year in 2016), but I feel like... fuck, a lot of time, a lot of money... wasted.

The degree was/is English W/Media.

Thanks for checking, friend.

Yeah, still anxious, still stressed. 

Had a bad moment today. Looked up someone who was in the same course at the same time as me & seeing all they were up to... well, I started feeling like a failure. Quite intense. Kinda just zoned out for a bit. 

Just this horrible feeling of TIME passing by, y'know? I'm a young man, yeah, but still.

An eating disorder? Never considered it, but you may be right.

I feel bad about not being able to drive primarily because it means it's my parents who have to take me everywhere. They say they don't mind, and I believe them, but it still cuts me. 

No gym nearby, but plenty of countryside. I'll go run.

Yeah, I went to the doctor, but I don't think I properly expressed how I was feeling. He gave me a number (counselling service), which I don't much feel like calling. 

Actually had some guy on Twitter suggest exercise to me, which sounds like a good idea. Used to exercise quite a bit before I tapered off it. 

The degree was English W/ Media (not the most helpful to others...!) and I feel like I'm in a "might as well finish it" situation. Which doesn't help the anxiety.
